Beer and service were excellent and the audience was Asian on both nights. We felt very comfortable.
Feb 2025 • Couples
Impressive restaurant on a slightly elevated covered terrace on the very pleasant tree-lined Pasteur Street.
You have to go up a few steps and then you see a very large and very friendly hall. Almost a beer garden milieu from which you have a beautiful view over the street. A mega screen where you could have watched football from GB didn't fit. We sat with our backs to this wall.
We stayed here two nights and drank only beer here. The latter was quite excellent. It came on tap, served in glass jugs, was well tapped and tasted quite excellent. The price was also moderate. The food was not expensive either, but the offer here was too strong European for us; we saw mountains of French fries. We love country cuisine on all our trips.

Would not go back!
Feb 2015
It appears to be very popular but our own experience would not get us going back. It was extremely loud and crowded; the waitress stared and waited right at our table while we were looking through the menu to choose our meals, it was very uncomfortable and we felt rushed. The meals were below average; I had steak (which came with two pieces of broccoli only) and my partner had grilled beef (which came with an unappetizing side of what seemed like pickled vegetables) -- neither meals tasted great. The prices were definitely high considering the quality and quantity of food we received. We did not use the wet naps provided on the table since most restaurants we've been to here in Vietnam leave the wet naps on the table but don't tell you you have to pay if you use them. When it came time to pay, we paid with US money. They gave us change in Vietnamese Dong (which is fine since that's what most restaurants do at the current (or close to) exchange rate). They gave us WAY less change and when we questioned why the waitress called her supervisor over and did not want to deal with us. The supervisor told us they have a lower in-house exchange rate...WAY lower. We argued for 15 minutes until she finally told us to take a cab to go to the bank to exchange the money since they didn't accept US money -- which made no sense since she accepted it the first time and we had received change. We ended up paying "their" rate after arguing some more because we were so annoyed and furious at this point. The waitress delivered our food and we never saw her again; it took us 10 minutes to get someone's attention so we could get our bill. Needless to say, we would never go back and do not recommend this restaurant. Much cheaper places in Saigon with better food, atmosphere and service -- don't waste your time... Or your money!

I did see someone eating something that looked great and was told that it was a radish sprout and beef salad. Maybe I'll try that next time. My fallback, if I'm desperately hungry is for french fries. Those have been consistently good, just not the best dinner fare. 
In the evening you can sit outside (good when it's not too hot) and literally watch the world go by. A fun pastime in my estimation. As with most places that are not 5 star hotels or reliable bars, I would skip any other alcoholic beverages except beer. We did purchase a bottle of wine there that was ok, but was a bit on the spendy side for what it was. If you're in the neighborhood, stop by for a beer! Tourist prices, thus $$ for the price rating. Average for US run of the mill places.

This is my absolute favorite place in Saigon to go for a beer (or two, or four...) after work. The beer comes in two styles, yellow and black.
